overview.problem: Users can track habits but cannot follow friends for accountability. The platform needs friend-only habit activity sharing while preserving strict privacy for all other health domains.
overview.goal: Deliver a secure social layer that supports friend relationships, a friends-only habit activity feed, and explicit privacy controls without leaking non-habit data.

inScope.item: Friend request lifecycle: send, accept, decline, remove, block.
Habit activity event generation and friend feed rendering.
Per-user social privacy settings for habit activity sharing.
API, storage, schema, and frontend support for social features.

outOfScope.item: Public profiles or discoverability by non-friends.
Sharing measurements, goals, nutrition, calculations, recipes, or imports/exports.
Comments, reactions, chat, and real-time push in v1.

requirements.functional: Friendship lifecycle management with anti-abuse and self/duplicate request protections.
Habit activity event capture on completion changes with minimal feed payload.
Friends-only reverse-chronological feed with cursor pagination (default 25, max 100).
Access boundaries that prevent cross-user exposure of non-habit domains.
Friends page UX with Feed, Friends, Requests, and Privacy tabs.

phase.name: Social Data Layer
phase.objective: Create the database tables, relations, indexes, and Drizzle migration for the entire social feature set.
phase.task: Define the `friendships` table in shared/schema.ts with columns (id, requesterPatientId, addresseePatientId, status enum, createdAt, respondedAt), unique pair constraint, and self-request check constraint.
Define the `habit_activity_events` table in shared/schema.ts with columns (id, actorPatientId, habitId, habitEntryId nullable, eventType enum, eventDate nullable, createdAt).
Define the `social_privacy_settings` table in shared/schema.ts with columns (patientId PK/FK, shareHabitActivity boolean default true, showHabitName boolean default true, updatedAt).
Add Drizzle `relations()` declarations linking social tables to `patients` and `habits`/`habit_entries`.
Add performance indexes: friendships (requester+status, addressee+status), habit_activity_events (createdAt desc, actorPatientId+createdAt desc).
Export insert schemas (Zod) and select types for all three new tables.
Generate and review the Drizzle migration file; verify it applies cleanly to a fresh local DB.
phase.deliverable: Three new social tables with relations, indexes, Zod schemas, and a verified migration.

phase.name: Friendship Lifecycle Backend
phase.objective: Ship the API that lets users send, accept, decline, remove, and block friends with full authorization enforcement.
phase.task: Add route contracts in shared/routes.ts for POST /api/social/friends/requests (send), GET /api/social/friends/requests (list incoming+outgoing), POST …/:id/accept, POST …/:id/decline, POST …/:id/block.
Add route contracts in shared/routes.ts for GET /api/social/friends (list accepted) and DELETE /api/social/friends/:friendPatientId (remove friend).
Extend IStorage interface with friendship methods: createFriendRequest, getFriendRequests, acceptFriendRequest, declineFriendRequest, blockFriendRequest, listFriends, removeFriend.

Implement friendship storage methods in DatabaseStorage, including: duplicate/self-request rejection, status transition validation (pending→accepted/declined/blocked), bidirectional lookup for removals, and block enforcement.
Register friendship API routes in server/routes.ts under isAuthenticated; wire request parsing with Zod schemas and call storage methods.
Write friendship-specific tests: send/accept/decline/remove happy paths, self-request rejection, duplicate request rejection, block prevents future requests, unauthorized access returns 403.
phase.deliverable: Complete friendship API with storage logic and test coverage for all state transitions.

phase.name: Habit Activity Event Capture
phase.objective: Automatically record habit_activity_events when users toggle habit completions, providing the raw data the feed consumes.
phase.task: Add IStorage method: createHabitActivityEvent(actorPatientId, habitId, habitEntryId, eventType, eventDate).
Implement createHabitActivityEvent in DatabaseStorage with a simple insert into habit_activity_events.
Hook event creation into the existing toggleHabitEntry flow: emit `habit_completed` when marking complete, `habit_uncompleted` when unmarking.
(Optional) Emit `habit_created` event when a new habit is created (default off; guard behind a feature flag or config constant).
Write tests: toggling a habit creates the correct event record; event fields match habit/entry data; no event is created for no-op toggles.
phase.deliverable: Habit activity events are reliably written on every completion state change, ready for feed consumption.

phase.name: Social Privacy Settings Backend
phase.objective: Let users manage shareHabitActivity and showHabitName preferences via API, with defaults auto-provisioned on first read.
phase.task: Add route contracts in shared/routes.ts for GET /api/social/privacy (read) and PUT /api/social/privacy (update).
Extend IStorage with getSocialPrivacySettings(patientId) and updateSocialPrivacySettings(patientId, data).
Implement storage methods in DatabaseStorage: get returns existing row or inserts+returns defaults; update performs upsert and sets updatedAt.
Register privacy API routes in server/routes.ts under isAuthenticated.
Write tests: default settings are returned for new user; update persists; partial update only changes specified fields; unauthorized access returns 403.
phase.deliverable: Privacy settings API with auto-provisioning and full test coverage.

phase.name: Friends Feed Endpoint
phase.objective: Expose a paginated, privacy-aware feed of accepted-friend habit activity events.
phase.task: Add route contract in shared/routes.ts for GET /api/social/feed with cursor and limit query params; define FeedItem response shape.
Add IStorage method: getFriendFeed(viewerPatientId, cursor, limit) returning { items: FeedItem[], nextCursor }.

Implement getFriendFeed in DatabaseStorage: - Join habit_activity_events with friendships (status=accepted) to scope to friends only. - Join social_privacy_settings to exclude actors with shareHabitActivity=false. - Conditionally omit habit title when actor's showHabitName=false. - Include minimal actor profile data (displayName, avatar). - Apply cursor-based pagination ordered by createdAt desc; default 25, max 100.
Add helper verifyFriendAccess(actorPatientId, viewerPatientId) to validate that viewer is an accepted friend and neither party is blocked; reuse in feed safety.
Register the feed API route in server/routes.ts under isAuthenticated.

Write feed-specific tests: - Feed returns only accepted-friend events. - Blocked users return zero items in both directions. - shareHabitActivity=false hides events. - showHabitName=false omits habit title. - Cursor pagination returns correct pages. - No non-habit data appears in response.
Performance baseline: measure p95 latency for 25-item feed with 100 friends against seeded data; document results.
phase.deliverable: Secure, paginated friends feed endpoint passing all privacy and access-control tests.

phase.name: Frontend Friends Page and Hooks
phase.objective: Build the Friends page with tab navigation and wire it to the social API via React Query hooks.
phase.task: Create client/src/hooks/use-social.ts with React Query hooks: useFriendFeed, useFriendsList, useFriendRequests, usePrivacySettings (query + mutation for each writable resource).
Create client/src/pages/Friends.tsx with tab-based layout containing four tabs: Feed, Friends, Requests, Privacy.
Add /friends route in client/src/App.tsx as a protected route (must be authenticated).
Add "Friends" nav entry in Sidebar.tsx with an appropriate icon.
phase.deliverable: Navigable Friends page shell with working routing and data-fetching hooks.

phase.name: Frontend Social Components
phase.objective: Build all social UI components and compose them into the Friends page tabs with proper state handling.
phase.task: Create client/src/components/social/FeedItem.tsx — renders a single activity event (actor avatar/name, event text, habit title when permitted, relative timestamp).
Create client/src/components/social/FeedList.tsx — renders the scrollable, paginated feed using useFriendFeed; handles infinite scroll or "Load more" with cursor.
Create client/src/components/social/FriendRequestCard.tsx — shows incoming/outgoing request with accept/decline/cancel actions.
Create client/src/components/social/SendRequestForm.tsx — email input to send a new friend request with validation and feedback.
Create client/src/components/social/FriendCard.tsx — renders an accepted friend with remove/block actions.
Create client/src/components/social/PrivacyForm.tsx — toggle switches for shareHabitActivity and showHabitName bound to usePrivacySettings mutation.
Implement empty states for each tab: "No friends yet" (Friends), "No activity yet" (Feed), "No pending requests" (Requests), "Sharing disabled" hint (Privacy when off).
Implement loading skeletons and error states for each tab using existing app patterns.
Wire all components into Friends.tsx tabs and verify end-to-end flow with backend.
phase.deliverable: Fully functional social UI with feed, friend management, request handling, and privacy controls.

phase.name: Polish, Guardrails, and Hardening
phase.objective: Refine UX copy, add anti-abuse safeguards, and prepare for broad rollout.
phase.task: Refine feed event copy: human-friendly text for each eventType (e.g., "Alice completed Morning Run", "Bob completed a habit").
Add micro-animations: feed item entrance, toggle transitions for privacy switches, request card accept/decline feedback.
Add rate limiting on friend request endpoints (e.g., max 20 requests/hour per user).
Evaluate and optionally implement a retention/archival policy for old habit_activity_events (e.g., soft-delete events older than 90 days).
Assess and optionally add a notification badge on the Friends nav item for pending incoming requests.
End-to-end integration test: create two users, send request, accept, toggle habit, verify feed shows event, toggle privacy off, verify event hidden, block, verify zero visibility.
Security audit checklist: verify no social endpoint leaks measurements/goals/nutrition; verify blocked users have zero bidirectional visibility; verify all endpoints require auth.
phase.deliverable: Hardened, polished social feature ready for broad rollout with anti-abuse safeguards and full E2E validation.

security.rule: All social endpoints require authenticated sessions.
Feed query must return only accepted-friend events and must respect block relationships.
Privacy settings are enforced at read-time to allow immediate visibility revocation.
No social response may include measurements, goals, nutrition, calculations, or recipe entities.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Users can complete friend request to accepted friend feed flow.
Feed shows accepted friends only and paginates correctly.
Turning off shareHabitActivity hides past and future events.
Blocked users have zero bidirectional feed visibility.
Feed p95 latency for 25 items and 100 friends is < 300ms.

metrics.metric: Percent of active users with at least one friend.
Average friend requests sent and accepted.

risk.description: Privacy regression due to social joins.
risk.mitigation: Centralize friendship and privacy filters in storage and enforce with test matrix.

risk.description: Feed bloat and query degradation over time.
risk.mitigation: Use cursor pagination and evaluate retention/archive strategy.
Rate limiting, block support, and duplicate/self-request prevention.

openQuestions.question: Should uncomplete actions appear in feed, or only completions?
Should old feed events remain visible after unfriending, or be hidden immediately?
Should habit titles be hidden by default for stricter privacy?
Should pending friend requests surface as a navigation badge in v1?
